title: Ideal source bits
statement: Let $M$ be a Turing machine with Boolean-valued symbols, let $x$ be a finite Boolean string, and let $t$ be a natural number. Define the source list by concatenating: if $t=0$, a list of $	ext{snapWidth}(M)$ false bits, and otherwise the encoding of the configuration of $M$ on $x$ at time $t-1$; the three bits indicating respectively that $t=0$, that the input head position at time $t$ on input $x$ contains an input bit, and the value of that bit (taken to be false if there is no such bit); the ideal tape-bit lists at time $t$ for each of the $M.k$ work tapes; and finally false if $t=0$, or the indicator that $M$ has accepted $x$ by time $t-1$ otherwise.
hypotheses_covered: A Turing machine $M$ with Boolean-valued symbols
caveat: The statement uses several upstream constructions that are not defined in the supplied payload; in particular, the exact meaning of the snapshot encoding, ideal tape-bit lists, and acceptance indicator is unavailable.
